raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Follow-up to the review on #38959. `PPConsensusStore` binds its PULL socket on `get_local_ip_auto()` (required for multi-node PP) with no authentication, and the receive loop called `pickle.loads` on whatever arrived. Two problems:

1. Anyone who can reach that port gets code execution in the PP0 prefill scheduler. The repo already treats this socket class as a hardening target (see the CVE-2026-3060 note on `get_zmq_socket_on_host`), and the rest of disaggregation avoids pickle on zmq.
2. The receive loop had no error handling, and the worker thread's catch-all runs `os._exit(1)`. A single garbage datagram (or a transient decode error) took down the whole PP0 prefill instance.

## Modifications

- Wire format is now a `msgspec.Struct(array_like=True)` of `(kind, rank, key, value)`, msgpack-encoded. Decoding is typed, so only that exact shape is accepted.
- `_decode` drops and logs messages that fail to decode, come from a rank outside `(0, pp_size)`, or carry an unknown op kind. The `os._exit(1)` path is kept for genuine internal failures but is no longer reachable from network input.
- Encoding moved to the caller's thread (`__setitem__` / `pop` / `__delitem__`), so an unencodable value raises at the call site and leaves the local map untouched, instead of killing the background sender.

## Test

`test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_pp_consensus_store.py` (base-a-test-cpu), three new cases:

- `test_malformed_messages_are_dropped`: pushes empty, invalid-msgpack, pickle, wrong-shape, rank-0, out-of-range-rank, unknown-op, bad-key-type and bad-value-type frames at the PP0 socket, then a valid PUT on the same connection, and asserts the PUT landed. Against the #38959 store this test kills the pytest process (exit 1, no output); with this change all 21 tests pass.
- `test_int_room_key_round_trip`: integer bootstrap-room keys survive the typed wire format.
- `test_unencodable_value_raises_in_caller`: the new encode-at-call-site contract.

Ran locally on CPU: 21 passed. black/isort clean.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

 """Unit tests for srt/disaggregation/pp_consensus_store."""
 
+import pickle
 import time
 import unittest
 from collections.abc import Callable
 
+import msgspec
+import zmq
+
 from sglang.srt.disaggregation.pp_consensus_store import PPConsensusStore
 from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
 from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
@@ -187,6 +191,54 @@ def test_collect_requires_pp0(self):
         store0.close()
         store1.close()
 
+    def test_int_room_key_round_trip(self):
+        group = _MockPPGroup()
+        store0 = PPConsensusStore(2, 0, group)
+        store1 = PPConsensusStore(2, 1, group)
+        room = 1234567890123
+        store1[room] = 2
+        self._wait_until(lambda: store0.collect(room) == [None, 2])
+        store1.pop(room)
+        self._wait_until(lambda: store0.collect(room) == [None, None])
+        store0.close()
+        store1.close()
+
+    def test_unencodable_value_raises_in_caller(self):
+        group = _MockPPGroup()
+        store0 = PPConsensusStore(2, 0, group)
+        store1 = PPConsensusStore(2, 1, group)
+        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
+            store1["key"] = object()
+        self.assertFalse("key" in store1)
+        store0.close()
+        store1.close()
+
+    def test_malformed_messages_are_dropped(self):
+        """Garbage on the PP0 socket must be dropped; it must never exit the process."""
+        group = _MockPPGroup()
+        store0 = PPConsensusStore(2, 0, group)
+        ctx = zmq.Context()
+        peer = ctx.socket(zmq.PUSH)
+        peer.connect(store0._socket.getsockopt_string(zmq.LAST_ENDPOINT))
+        for raw in (
+            b"",
+            b"\xc1",  # invalid msgpack
+            pickle.dumps((1, 1, "key", 99)),
+            msgspec.msgpack.encode({"kind": 1}),
+            msgspec.msgpack.encode([1, 0, "key", 99]),  # rank 0 never sends
+            msgspec.msgpack.encode([1, 7, "key", 99]),  # rank out of range
+            msgspec.msgpack.encode([9, 1, "key", 99]),  # unknown op
+            msgspec.msgpack.encode([1, 1, ["key"], 99]),  # bad key type
+            msgspec.msgpack.encode([1, 1, "key", "bad"]),  # bad value type
+        ):
+            peer.send(raw)
+        # Same connection, so this lands only after every message above was handled.
+        peer.send(msgspec.msgpack.encode([1, 1, "key", 11]))
+        self._wait_until(lambda: store0.collect("key") == [None, 11])
+        peer.close(linger=0)
+        ctx.term()
+        store0.close()
+
 
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     unittest.main()
